samples.summary: A second handover from the same page overwrites the first bundle.json (data loss)
samples.evidence: The write path is `path.join(repoRoot, '.wb-reports', bundle.sessionId, 'bundle.json')` with `writeFileSync` (no uniqueness, no append). `sessionId` is `DEBUG_SESSION_ID`, a module-level constant created once per page load (`src/ui/session-id.ts:37`) and passed unchanged to every `handOver` call via `DebugOverlay`'s `sessionId` prop (`mount.tsx`, `panel.tsx:168`). The design *expects* multiple handovers per page: `withinSessionCap` queues PRs past 5 and the panel tells the reporter they are "waiting for the next batch", then keeps `result.queuedItems` in the session for a second send. That second send lands in the same directory and replaces the first `bundle.json` — and the first batch's items were already dropped from the session on success (`panel.tsx:178`), so those reports are unrecoverable if intake had not yet consumed the file. Its capture images are also left behind, referenced by nothing.

samples.summary: No timeout on the report POST, so a stalled dev server leaves the panel stuck in "Sending…" forever
samples.evidence: `send()` calls `postJson(REPORT_ENDPOINT, {bundle, captures})` with no `timeoutMs`, so `controller`/`timer` are undefined and neither the header wait nor the body read can be abandoned. The draft path passes `DRAFT_TIMEOUT_MS` with the comment "Without this the panel could wait forever: a dev server stopped mid-flight leaves the promise unsettled, and the batch un-sendable" — the same failure applies with more force to the send, and the panel's `sending` flag stays `true` (`panel.tsx:162`/`183`) so the Hand over button is permanently disabled with no message.

samples.summary: `send()` has `try/finally` but no `catch`: a rejection from handOver fails silently with an unhandled rejection
samples.evidence: `const send = async () => { ... try { const result = await handOver(...) ... } finally { setSending(false) } }`, invoked as `onClick={() => void send()}`. `handOver` can reject: `options.store.getCapture` is inside `Promise.all` (handover.ts:191) and an IndexedDB read failure rejects, as can `host.environment()` and `host.send`. On rejection no `report` is set, nothing is sent, and the reporter sees the button simply re-enable with no explanation — the exact silent no-op the overlay's own `run()` helper was written to avoid — plus an unhandled promise rejection on `window`.

samples.summary: An item the model produced no draft for is silently withheld from the batch and never reported as queued
samples.evidence: `normaliseGroups` only creates solo groups for items that have a draft (`draft.ts:263` iterates `drafts`), so an item the model omitted (or whose duplicate draft was dropped) ends up in no group at all. In `handOver`, `grouped` is true, `sending` does not contain that id, so it lands in `queuedItems` and is excluded from `bundle.items` — while `result.queued` stays empty, so `handoverReport` prints no "stayed queued" line. The reporter clicked "Hand over 3 report(s)", 2 travel, and nothing says why the third did not.

samples.summary: A capture that could not be read is reported to the reporter but the bundle still claims it, so intake gets a bundle referencing an image that is not on disk
samples.evidence: `missingCaptures.push(read.note)` only records the note; `bundle.items` still carries the full `capture` metadata (id/w/h/bytes/mime) and the endpoint writes `bundle.json` with it while no matching `<id>.jpg` was ever sent. `report-endpoint.ts:151` states this exact hazard as the reason decoding and writing are separated ("a bundle written next to a refused capture would be picked up by intake while referencing an image that is not on disk"), and this client path produces precisely that state — the all-or-nothing guard only covers `refused`, not `missing`.

samples.summary: `store.sweep()` runs before the session save commits, so the sent batch's blobs are not the ones swept
samples.evidence: `session.replaceAll(result.queuedItems)` schedules a React update; the `store.save(DEBUG_SESSION_ID, items)` that rewrites `localStorage` only runs in `useDebugSession`'s effect after the next commit (`use-debug-session.ts:127`). `sweep()` is invoked synchronously on the next line and reads `readPersisted()` (store.ts:530), which still lists the just-sent items, so their blobs count as referenced and survive. The stated purpose — "Orphan images otherwise fill the eviction budget, and the next capture evicts a LIVE one" — is not achieved until some later sweep.

samples.summary: Sending before the draft arrives bypasses the per-session PR cap entirely
samples.evidence: The footer deliberately keeps the Hand over button enabled while `draftState.status === 'asking'`, at which point `groups` is still `[]`. `handOver` then computes `alive = []`, `grouped = false`, and sends every kept item with `groups: []` — `withinSessionCap` never constrains anything, so a 20-item session goes over in one bundle with no grouping, which is what the MAX_SESSION_PRS ceiling exists to prevent.

samples.summary: `ungrouped()` labels every group `logic`, and the label is what the pipeline routes on
samples.evidence: `kind: 'logic' as ChangeKind` for every item on the no-credential path. draft.ts:242-246 argues at length that "THE GROUP'S KIND COMES FROM ITS MEMBERS... a wrong one sends a spacing cleanup down the behaviour-fix path"; the degraded path unconditionally applies the one label the rules treat as never-groupable to appearance reports as well.

samples.summary: Escape does not close the review panel while focus is in one of the panel's own fields
samples.evidence: The keydown handler returns early when `isTypingTarget(e.target)` (true for the panel's note/title/body inputs), before `actionWhileReviewing` is consulted. The panel's inputs also `e.stopPropagation()` in `onKeyDown` but that cannot suppress the window capture-phase listener anyway, and they do not handle Escape themselves — so "Close (Esc)", which the panel header advertises, is dead whenever a field is focused.

samples.summary: Base64 payload is never validated before being written, so a malformed capture is silently written as a corrupt image
samples.evidence: `Buffer.from(dataUrl.slice(comma + 1), 'base64')` ignores invalid characters and truncates rather than failing, so a truncated or garbled data URL passes the header regex and is written to disk as a short/corrupt file. Since the response is 200, the reporter is told the handover succeeded and the session is cleared, leaving intake with an unreadable image and no signal.

samples.summary: Opening the panel with an empty session shows a "Drafting did not answer" error rather than the empty state
samples.evidence: `requestDrafts` returns `{status:'unavailable', reason:'empty', detail:'nothing collected yet'}` for zero items, and `DraftBanner` renders anything not `not-configured` as "Drafting did not answer (empty: nothing collected yet)" — an error message for a state that is not an error. Reachable by pressing `v` before collecting anything.

finding.summary: A second handover from the same page overwrites the first bundle.json (data loss)
finding.evidence: The write path is `path.join(repoRoot, '.wb-reports', bundle.sessionId, 'bundle.json')` with `writeFileSync` (no uniqueness, no append). `sessionId` is `DEBUG_SESSION_ID`, a module-level constant created once per page load (`src/ui/session-id.ts:37`) and passed unchanged to every `handOver` call via `DebugOverlay`'s `sessionId` prop (`mount.tsx`, `panel.tsx:168`). The design *expects* multiple handovers per page: `withinSessionCap` queues PRs past 5 and the panel tells the reporter they are "waiting for the next batch", then keeps `result.queuedItems` in the session for a second send. That second send lands in the same directory and replaces the first `bundle.json` — and the first batch's items were already dropped from the session on success (`panel.tsx:178`), so those reports are unrecoverable if intake had not yet consumed the file. Its capture images are also left behind, referenced by nothing.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. report-endpoint.ts:257-265 writes to `<repoRoot>/.wb-reports/<bundle.sessionId>/bundle.json` with a fixed filename via writeFileSync — no uniqueness suffix, no existence check (`wx`), no merge. sessionId is a module-level constant created once per page load (ui/session-id.ts:37) and threaded unchanged into every send (frontend/src/debug/mount.tsx:42 -> panel.tsx:164-171 -> handover.ts:182-188 buildBundle). Multiple handovers per page load are the intended design, not an edge case: handover.ts:160 applies withinSessionCap and returns `queued`/`queuedItems`, handoverSummary (handover.ts:233) says "N waiting for the next batch", and on success the panel keeps only the unsent items (panel.tsx:178 session.replaceAll(result.queuedItems); panel.tsx:180 setGroups(result.queued)) — so the first batch's items are already dropped from client state when the second send lands in the same directory and replaces bundle.json. Nothing guards this: ui/host.ts:182 posts the bundle verbatim, bundle.ts:44 just copies sessionId, and the intake runner named in the design (docs/design/debug-report.md:90, scripts/agent/report-*.mjs) does not exist in the tree, so no consumer has moved the file away — the header comment at report-endpoint.ts:6-8 confirms "the file is the handover". The first batch's capture images are also left orphaned since only the surviving bundle references captures. Real, reachable, unrecoverable data loss — critical under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: No timeout on the report POST, so a stalled dev server leaves the panel stuck in "Sending…" forever
finding.evidence: `send()` calls `postJson(REPORT_ENDPOINT, {bundle, captures})` with no `timeoutMs`, so `controller`/`timer` are undefined and neither the header wait nor the body read can be abandoned. The draft path passes `DRAFT_TIMEOUT_MS` with the comment "Without this the panel could wait forever: a dev server stopped mid-flight leaves the promise unsettled, and the batch un-sendable" — the same failure applies with more force to the send, and the panel's `sending` flag stays `true` (`panel.tsx:162`/`183`) so the Hand over button is permanently disabled with no message.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: postJson only arms an AbortController/timer when timeoutMs is supplied (ui/host.ts:61-65,72), and send() calls it with no timeoutMs (ui/host.ts:182), unlike draft() which passes DRAFT_TIMEOUT_MS (ui/host.ts:169). A server that accepts the connection but never answers leaves the header await (line 68) or the body read (line 92) pending forever. Searched the whole debug-report src for setTimeout/AbortController/timeout/race — no other guard exists; handover.ts:210 awaits host.send bare, and panel.tsx:162-184 resets `sending` only in a finally that never runs, so the Hand over button stays disabled showing "Sending…" with no message (panel.tsx:297-304). Also checked the sole construction site (frontend/src/debug/mount.tsx:37) for a timeout-wrapping decorator and any global fetch override — none apply. No counterexample found.

finding.summary: `send()` has `try/finally` but no `catch`: a rejection from handOver fails silently with an unhandled rejection
finding.evidence: `const send = async () => { ... try { const result = await handOver(...) ... } finally { setSending(false) } }`, invoked as `onClick={() => void send()}`. `handOver` can reject: `options.store.getCapture` is inside `Promise.all` (handover.ts:191) and an IndexedDB read failure rejects, as can `host.environment()` and `host.send`. On rejection no `report` is set, nothing is sent, and the reporter sees the button simply re-enable with no explanation — the exact silent no-op the overlay's own `run()` helper was written to avoid — plus an unhandled promise rejection on `window`.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I found no counterexample. panel.tsx:160-185 defines `send` with try/finally and no catch, invoked fire-and-forget at panel.tsx:292 (onClick={() => void send()}). No wrapper adds handling: the overlay's catching `run()` helper (overlay.tsx:138-152) is used only for captures, `handOver` has no internal try/catch (handover.ts:145-212), and there is no error boundary or `unhandledrejection` listener on the debug-report/frontend mount path (frontend/src/debug/mount.tsx:29-46; the only such listener in the repo is design-editor/src/scenes/scene-entry.tsx:123, a different surface). The reviewer's specific mechanism is partly wrong, which is why I considered refuting on already-guarded: the production store swallows IndexedDB read failures (store.ts:503-509, surfaced as missingCaptures at handover.ts:204-208), createDevHost().send returns {ok:false} rather than rejecting (ui/host.ts:56-115, 178-198), environment() is pure reads (ui/host.ts:133-145, bundle.ts:98-108), and sweep() catches (store.ts:529-545). But that refutation would be unsound: session.replaceAll at panel.tsx:178 runs inside the try and notify() deliberately RETHROWS the first subscriber error (session.ts:110-127, throw firstError at :126), and both HostAdapter.send (host.ts:83, an explicit SP2 substitution seam) and CaptureStore.getCapture (store.ts:308) are interfaces whose implementations may reject, with DebugPanel publicly exported (ui/index.ts:21). The package's own standard is to catch and tell the reporter (requestDrafts, handover.ts:46-78). On rejection no report is set, nothing is sent, the finally silently re-enables the button, and the rejection escapes to window. Impact is narrower than claimed but real, and no named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: An item the model produced no draft for is silently withheld from the batch and never reported as queued
finding.evidence: `normaliseGroups` only creates solo groups for items that have a draft (`draft.ts:263` iterates `drafts`), so an item the model omitted (or whose duplicate draft was dropped) ends up in no group at all. In `handOver`, `grouped` is true, `sending` does not contain that id, so it lands in `queuedItems` and is excluded from `bundle.items` — while `result.queued` stays empty, so `handoverReport` prints no "stayed queued" line. The reporter clicked "Hand over 3 report(s)", 2 travel, and nothing says why the third did not.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. draft.ts:263 builds leftover solo groups by iterating `drafts`, so an item the model omitted (omission is not an error — parseDraftResult only validates present entries, draft.ts:144-186) or whose duplicate draft was dropped (draft.ts:154-157) belongs to no group. In handOver (handover.ts:169-180) `grouped` is true because other items produced groups, `sending` lacks that id, so it is filtered out of `items`/`bundle.items` and pushed into `queuedItems`. handoverReport (handover.ts:243-255) prints the "stayed queued" line only from `result.queued`, which is the session-cap overflow list from withinSessionCap (draft.ts:427-432) and is empty in this scenario, so nothing explains the missing report; meanwhile handoverSummary/summariseBundle (handover.ts:219, bundle.ts:63-79) counted the item, so the pre-send line said 3 reports. DraftBanner (panel.tsx:322-330) renders nothing when `dropped` is empty, so the plain-omission case has no UI signal either, and panel.tsx:109-114 uses outcome.groups verbatim with no re-add of undrafted items (the ungrouped() fallback at handover.ts:60 only fires when drafting is entirely unavailable). Not permanent data loss (panel.tsx:178 keeps queuedItems), but a silent withholding with a misleading report — a real correctness/reporting bug.

finding.summary: A capture that could not be read is reported to the reporter but the bundle still claims it, so intake gets a bundle referencing an image that is not on disk
finding.evidence: `missingCaptures.push(read.note)` only records the note; `bundle.items` still carries the full `capture` metadata (id/w/h/bytes/mime) and the endpoint writes `bundle.json` with it while no matching `<id>.jpg` was ever sent. `report-endpoint.ts:151` states this exact hazard as the reason decoding and writing are separated ("a bundle written next to a refused capture would be picked up by intake while referencing an image that is not on disk"), and this client path produces precisely that state — the all-or-nothing guard only covers `refused`, not `missing`.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: handOver builds the bundle at handover.ts:182-188 with full `capture` metadata, then reads captures at handover.ts:191-208; an unreadable capture only appends a note string to `missingCaptures` (line 207) and never removes `item.capture` from the bundle. The unmodified bundle plus the partial captures array is sent at handover.ts:210 (host contract host.ts:83 does no stripping). On the server, report-endpoint.ts:248-255 only rejects the whole handover for `refused` captures returned by `prepareCaptures`; a capture that was never sent is indistinguishable from "no capture", so mkdir/writeFileSync at report-endpoint.ts:257-265 persists bundle.json referencing an image file that was never written. The endpoint's own doc comment (report-endpoint.ts:168-176) names this exact hazard as the reason decode and write are separated. handover.test.ts:121-131 exercises the case and confirms the send proceeds. No guard elsewhere reconciles bundle capture ids with delivered capture names, so this is a real broken invariant / persisted-inconsistency defect in the correctness lane.
